entryAnswer.explanation:
Design and evidence.

Entry contract. `spendingAlertsFor(graph, defaults)` binds immutable defaults and returns a frozen `{ compose }`; configuration allocates no graph nodes, and each `compose` invokes the existing complete host construction (causal-entry.ts:48-77). `configuration` validates name (non-empty, <=256) and diagnostics ("off"|"summary"), inheriting defaults when an override field is undefined (causal-entry.ts:36-46). So one shared defaults object `{ name: "alerts", diagnostics: "off" }` is passed once, and per-compose overrides select only name/diagnostics (README.md:82-86).

Two independent instances. `compose(inputs, overrides)` validates the four exact input groups and the prepared resource via `SpendingResource.is` (causal-entry.ts:52-58), then calls `composeSpendingHost(graph, inputs, resource.binding, resource, options)` (causal-entry.ts:59-69). The host validates the binding against the resource binding, prepares a construction scope with the instance name, claims the resource lease, seals/transfers the owner, and starts construction (causal-focused-host.ts:67-126). Distinct names produce distinct node names (`spendingNodeNames(name, diagnostics)`, causal-preset.ts:60-72) and distinct input Nodes/resource bindings (README.md:85-86). The demo shows the same pattern: instance A composed with defaults, instance B composed with `{ name: "alerts-b" }` and its own input Nodes and its own resource (causal-graded-demo.ts:57-64, 88-114).

Diagnostics only for the second. `spendingNodeNames` appends `${name}/diagnosticSummary` only when `diagnostics === "summary"` (causal-preset.ts:70), and `buildSpendingPresetNodes` creates the `diagnosticSummary` node only in that case (causal-preset.ts:180-190). Passing `diagnostics: "summary"` only in the second override therefore enables summary diagnostics for the second instance alone; the first inherits "off".

Render callbacks. `mountSpendingView(view, render)` subscribes to the five ports of the original view, publishes latest values plus explicit `unavailable` ports, and returns a function that ends observation only (causal-view-binding.ts:16-56). Each instance is connected to its own callback through its own `app.view`; the ordinary panel is exactly this pattern (causal-ordinary-panel.ts:5-7).

What the application must retain after either display is unmounted. The returned cleanup function only unsubscribes; "Run ownership stays with the application" (causal-view-binding.ts:16, 32-36). Panel detach stops observation while the running instance retains outstanding obligations (README.md:104). Concretely the application must keep, for each instance: the composed host result `app` (its `owner`/`owner.instance`, `guard`, `source`, `runEndReady`, `built`, and `inspect`), the original `view` and `capabilities` (including `capabilities.execution` and `capabilities.retained.execution`), and the prepared `SpendingResource`/lease lineage. The demo keeps `app.owner` and `app.inspect` and shows that after detaching A's panel, A still has one in-flight write and one retained record, and that A completes while detached (causal-graded-demo.ts:65, 140-148, 181-192). Retained request records (including refusals) and unknown/reconcile-required outcomes must be preserved rather than treated as recovered by panel cleanup (README.md:107-112). `runEndReady`/`inspect().normalEndReady` are readiness conditions, not proof of lifecycle termination or resource release (README.md:105).

Scope discipline. The function does not create input Nodes, does not construct resources, does not open files, and does not call any transport; it only composes and mounts observation. Normal host behavior (including its simulated writer) is left intact.
